paragraphs.text: Wall is a creature type representing various barriers including walls ( 54 cards ); fences ( 2 cards ); doors or gates ( 11 cards ); or even magical shields or forcefields ( 6 cards ). Occasionally, siege structures like trebuchets ( 3 cards ) are also included in this type.

Walls appear in all colors . Walls appear predominantly in white and blue followed by red , green , black . While many colorless walls have been printed, there are less colorless walls than the individual amount of white or blue-aligned walls.
Walls were introduced in Alpha , which featured ten walls across all colors.

Walls were removed for a short time after Eighth Edition for due to flavor reasons (see "Flavor issues" below). However, walls returned in Tenth Edition where they were printed in each color, except black . Walls are used much more sparingly now, and Creative tries to keep them from feeling like inanimate objects.
Being unable to attack , Walls in general have a higher toughness than power (if not 0 power ) but there are exceptions, like Illusionary Wall or Blistering Barrier .

In a sense, it was hard to fathom how a Wall of Wood which seemed stationary would be able to move to block a creature. From a flavor perspective, a wall is either an artifact or land. With this in mind, Mark Rosewater and Brady Dommermuth spearheaded their removal from the game for several years.
Although Walls didn't make much sense creature-wise, they did have an über-logic to them in that they were used as a means to protect the player.
The meta-flavor was beloved by enough of R&D that Walls returned. The reallowance of Walls into the game was partially inspired by the temporary demise and return of Demons .
Originally, being a Wall implicitly did not allow the creature to attack.

With the release of Champions of Kamigawa the Wall type no longer prevented creatures from attacking, with the effect being taken over by the new defender keyword. This change also meant that changing the subtype of a creature to "Wall" no longer stops them from attacking. Previously printed Walls recieved an errata giving them defender .
Commander 2019 introduced the first legendary wall Pramikon, Sky Rampart . A legendary wall wouldn't appear again until The Walls of Ba Sing Se in Avatar: The Last Airbender .
With the exception of creatures with Changeling , no new Walls have been printed without Defender.
From the glossary of the Comprehensive Rules (September 25, 2026— Reality Fracture )

Tidal Wave originally created Wave tokens that "counted as Walls" so as it get their implicit rules prior to Defender being introduced. Similarly Basalt Golem created Stone tokens that also counted as wall. Eventually with the digital release of Mirage , both of these types were given errata so they were just Wall tokens with Defender.
Originally, the Wall creature type implicitly prevented creature with the type from attacking. This made Wall the only creature type having a specific rule attached to it.

Having this rule attached to the Wall type meant that cards like Mistform Ultimus ( Legions ) or Artificial Evolution were forced to have a specific non-wall condition to avoid preventing Mistform Ultimatus or the creatures whose type was changed by Artificial Evolution from attacking. This mechanic implicit ability would become defender in the Kamigawa block .
Testament of Faith is an enchantment that can become a X/X Wall Enchantment creature with defender.

Wall of Mulch is closest thing to a wall lord " as well as being the first wall that rewarded players for putting it in a deck with other Walls. While some cards in Rise of the Eldrazi have similar effects, they are dependent on Defenders rather than Walls themselves.
Sunscape Familiar has been used in various decks to reduce the mana cost of blue and green spells.
